claim: The Creator Mental Health Study by Creators 4 Mental Health, in partnership with Lupiani Insights & Strategies, surveyed 542 full-time and part-time creators across North America (published November 2025) and found 62% experience burnout - a genuinely independent instrument from the Billion Dollar Boy/Censuswide survey.
stance_target: prevalence of self-reported creator burnout - independent second instrument alongside BDB
scope_conditions: Cross-sectional survey of ACTIVE full-time and part-time creators (n=542); measures self-reported distress among survivors and cannot observe anyone who already quit content creation. North America only (US/Canada implied) - no Southeast Asia coverage. Sponsor-funded by Opus, BeReal, Social Currant, Statusphere, and The AAKOMA Project; Opus is a disclosed Tubefilter partner, so the outlet reporting on it is not fully neutral. Sampling frame, recruitment method, and exact field dates are not disclosed in this write-up or the study's own landing page.
quoted_support: "the researchers surveyed 542 full and part-time creators across North America... 62% of respondents said they experience burnout."

claim: 89% of the 542 surveyed creators claim to lack access to specialized mental health resources or benefits, and 69% report financial insecurity as a result of their work.
stance_target: financial instability and lack of institutional support as documented burnout/quitting-adjacent pressures on creators
scope_conditions: Same n=542 North American active-creator sample; self-reported access/insecurity, not a benefits-registry or administrative measure. Cannot be generalized outside North America.
quoted_support: "A whopping 89% of the surveyed individuals claimed to lack access to specialized mental health resources and benefits... 69% reported financial insecurity as a result of their work."

claim: 10% of surveyed creators reported having suicidal thoughts related to their work - roughly twice the NIMH-reported US adult rate, per Tubefilter's framing.
stance_target: severity of mental-health toll among creators
scope_conditions: Self-reported measure among n=542 active North American creators; comparison to NIMH adult population rate is the reporting outlet's own framing, not a matched case-control study. Should be treated as a serious but single cross-sectional estimate, not a trend.
quoted_support: "10% of survey respondents said they have had suicidal thoughts related to their work. That's twice the U.S. adult rate provided by the NIMH."

claim: Burnout and mental-health distress prevalence rise among creators who have been active for five or more years - a duration gradient not reported by the Billion Dollar Boy survey.
stance_target: tenure/duration effects on creator burnout, relevant to time-to-quit dynamics
scope_conditions: Reported only qualitatively in this write-up (no specific percentage by tenure band given); n=542, North America only. This is the only duration-gradient finding located in this batch, but it measures distress intensifying WITH tenure among survivors, not a hazard/exit rate.
quoted_support: "These issues become more common for creators who have been active for at least five years."

claim: The 62% burnout figure from Creators4MentalHealth (n=542, North America, Nov 2025) and the 52% figure from Billion Dollar Boy/Censuswide (n=1,000, US+UK, July 2025) are two independent burnout-prevalence estimates that bracket a bare majority, with the gap plausibly explained by differing question wording and inclusion of part-time creators in the C4MH sample.
stance_target: convergence/divergence across the two genuinely independent burnout prevalence studies in this batch
scope_conditions: Cross-study comparison finding. BDB asks about burnout 'as a direct result of your career' among a broader US+UK sample; C4MH asks a more general burnout question among North American full+part-time creators. Neither reports a comparable quit-intention or attrition figure to the other (C4MH reports no quit-intention rate at all, so it does not corroborate BDB's 37%).
quoted_support: "62% here versus 52% in BDB (n=1,000, US+UK, July 2025) are the two independent burnout prevalence estimates in this cluster, and they bracket a majority." [note author's cross-study synthesis]
